description: The app's calls: unknown ids, unsupported calls, end, list.

cases.description: an id the store does not hold is a refusal
machine.end ends the machine and emits machine:ended
a call the provider's can does not enable is a refusal
stop on a spot machine is a refusal
machine.list filters by kind
machine.get reads the provider
a machine the provider no longer has comes back ended
machine.get of an id the store does not hold is null
machine.wait polls until the status
machine.wait past its timeout is a refusal
machine.wait stops when the machine is ended
disk.wait gives the disk once ready
a disk call without can.disk is a refusal
a kind name not in the config is a refusal
machine.list with a kind not in the config is a refusal
machine.wait for a status that is not one is a refusal
machine.wait with a timeout that is not a dur is a refusal
port.open adds a rule, with its id; port.list gives it
an equal rule the machine has is given back, with no provider call
port.close removes a rule
port.close of a rule the machine does not have is done
from any opens two rules, IPv4 then IPv6, and gives back both
a match by port closes every rule of that port, and gives them back
a match by port and proto closes only rules of that proto; an absent proto is tcp
a match from any closes the rules open to anywhere, IPv4 and IPv6
a match without a key, or with one that is not a rule's, is a refusal
a rule that is not one is a refusal
a disk only grows: a size not above it now is a refusal
a machine starts with its kind's ports, and only those
a machine a recover makes starts with its kind's ports too
from any in a kind's ports starts the machine with two rules
a rule in a kind's ports that is not one is a refusal
ports on a kind whose provider has no can.port is a refusal
a kind without a distro boots ubuntu at its default version
a distro without a version boots its default version
a distro with a version boots that version
an entry's image is used in place of the kind's distro
a kind without a script gives none
a script is kept as it is, in the first-boot script, run once

scripts:
#!/bin/bash
# rig: the kind's first boot, once, as root
[ -e /var/lib/rig/boot.ran ] && exit 0
mkdir -p /var/lib/rig /var/log/rig
chmod 700 /var/lib/rig /var/log/rig
touch /var/lib/rig/boot.ran
exec >>/var/log/rig/boot.log 2>&1
trap 'echo $? > /var/lib/rig/boot.exit' EXIT
set -eo pipefail
echo 'ZWNobyBoaQo=' | base64 -d > /var/lib/rig/script
chmod 700 /var/lib/rig/script
if head -n 1 /var/lib/rig/script | grep -q '^#!'; then /var/lib/rig/script; else bash /var/lib/rig/script; fi

cases.description: a login goes to the distro's login user, and the machine shows it

scripts:
#!/bin/bash
# rig: the kind's first boot, once, as root
[ -e /var/lib/rig/boot.ran ] && exit 0
mkdir -p /var/lib/rig /var/log/rig
chmod 700 /var/lib/rig /var/log/rig
touch /var/lib/rig/boot.ran
exec >>/var/log/rig/boot.log 2>&1
trap 'echo $? > /var/lib/rig/boot.exit' EXIT
set -eo pipefail
id -u debian >/dev/null 2>&1 || useradd -m -s /bin/bash debian
[ "$(id -u debian)" -ge 1000 ] || { echo "rig: debian is a system user" >&2; exit 1; }
home=$(getent passwd debian | cut -d: -f6)
mkdir -p "$home/.ssh"
echo 'c3NoLWVkMjU1MTkgQUFBQUMzTnphQzFsWkRJMU5URTVBQUFBSUFiYyBtZUBsYXB0b3AKc3NoLXJzYSBBQUFBQjNOemFDMXljMkVBQUFBREFRQUIK' | base64 -d >> "$home/.ssh/authorized_keys"
chmod 700 "$home/.ssh"
chmod 600 "$home/.ssh/authorized_keys"
chown -R debian: "$home/.ssh"
echo 'debian ALL=(ALL) NOPASSWD:ALL' > /etc/sudoers.d/rig-login
chmod 440 /etc/sudoers.d/rig-login
